column15: Verified via the distillery's own product page and Wikipedia: Chatham, Kent, England; its whisky brand is Masthouse single malt, full flavour notes (vanilla, toffee apple, sweet cream, nutty/peppery finish) with no smoke, so peatProfile=none. Also makes Dockyard gin and Vela vodka (not whisky). No "Masthouse" row exists in this batch to parent despite the seed's note referencing one.

Confirmed via its own dedicated site: Virginia Distillery Company's American single malt line (Signature/Bourbon Cask/Cuvee Cask/Sherry Cask), no peat/smoke stated. Corrected parentSlug from "virginia-distillery-company" to "virginia-distillery" to match this batch's slug for that row.

Owner confirmed via the brand owner's own site (the seed could not confirm this): Quintessential Brands Group. Blend of single malt and grain Irish whiskey, bourbon-cask matured, no peat/smoke stated -- ordinary unpeated Irish blend.

Verified via own site: Co. Down, Northern Ireland, est. 2013; flagship brand Dunville's plus other lines (The Beginning, Weavers Spirits, Matt Darcy, Old Comber), sherry-cask emphasis, no peat/smoke stated. Coded IE since the Irish Whiskey GI covers the whole island and the closed country list has no separate Northern Ireland code. Range spans multiple whisky styles so defaultTypeName left empty.

Verified via Wikipedia: runs White Oak distillery in Akashi, Japan, "Akashi" branded whisky since 2007. Range spans single malt and blended releases (see takumi in this batch, resolved to Akashi Takumi), so defaultTypeName left empty. Peat not stated in the source, left unknown. Dropped the seed's claim that a "Tokinoka" row in this batch needs this as parent -- no such row exists in batch-19.

Identified this session (the seed could not find it): New Era Spirits' "Element Irish Whiskey", an "Open Innovation" brand launched 2022, flagship Fusion Series R/1.0 a 43% blend of single malt and single grain whiskey matured in ex-bourbon/oak/oloroso sherry/stout casks; also Lore (single malt) and X series. No peat/smoke stated in any series. Alias kept at brand scope only per the seed's reasoning (collision risk with "Element Fusion"/"Element Lore" as in-name matches, and with the unrelated "Elements of Islay"/"M&H Elements"/"Glenmorangie Elementa" already in the catalogue).

Holyrood distillery (Edinburgh, Lowland; David Robertson, ex-Macallan, is a co-founder) and Embra as part of its 2024-25 Founding Series confirmed via Wikipedia. Positive peat is well attested by press (bite-magazine.com quotes distillery manager Calum Rae on "heavily peated malt" giving "bold smoky flavours", though the finish is described as light; other retailers label it "lightly peated") but holyrooddistillery.co.uk itself returned 403 to both WebFetch and the browser this session, so no producer-domain page was opened -- keeping peatProfile=unknown per this round's rule rather than the seed's "medium" guess. Withheld peat proposal: light-to-medium per bite-magazine.com; a reviewer who can reach holyrooddistillery.co.uk/embra/ directly should confirm.
Verified via own site: Teurastamo, Helsinki, Finland; founded 2014, first distillery in Helsinki in over a century. No whisky-specific tasting notes found to confirm or rule out peat, left unknown.

Verified via the maker's own site: Fauconnier (Marconne, France), a blend of 15 single malt and grain whiskies matured 3 years, distilled/aged in Scotland; flavour notes are woody/vanilla/orchard fruit with no peat or smoke.

Verified via own site: Crestwood, KY (Oldham County), founded 2012 by Steve Thompson/Chris Miller/Mike Loring as Kentucky's first contract distillery. Corrected defaultTypeName from the seed's "rye": the site shows it distills under multiple brand names (Jefferson's Reserve, Whiskey Row Bourbon, Kentucky Artisan Distillery Series) besides Coalition's rye, so it is not rye-only -- left empty. No peat mentioned; American contract distilling essentially never uses peated malt.

Corrected owner: scotchwhisky.com's whiskypedia (opened this session) states King Robert II is produced by Ian Macleod Distillers Ltd (owned since a 1968 acquisition of William Maxwell (Scotch Whisky) Ltd), not "Angus Dundee Distillers" as the seed had it -- no source found connecting Angus Dundee to this brand. Ordinary NAS blended Scotch; the same source contrasts it with Ian Macleod's own dedicated peated brand Smokehead, supporting peatProfile=none. Roman numeral "Ii" spelling preserved verbatim in aliases.

Confirmed via Redwood Empire's own site: "Lost Monarch Small Batch Craft Whiskey Blend" (bourbon and rye blend), one of its everyday releases. No peat/smoke mentioned. Added a new "redwood-empire" row to this batch's producer.tsv since it wasn't in live-slugs.txt or elsewhere in this batch.

The seed found no web presence; this session found it is a real product sold across several export markets (Canada, Kenya) as a 7/10/12-year-old range at 40% ABV, with Scotland stated as its country of origin on the retailer page opened -- corrected countryCode from XX to GB-SCT. No bottler/producer name found on any listing; treated as an ordinary export blended Scotch (no peat mentioned) by the same convention used for King Robert II/Highland's Friends in this batch.

Annandale's own site (opened) confirms Man O' Sword as its peated single-cask range, named for Robert the Bruce, opposite the unpeated Man O' Words (named for Robert Burns); Wikipedia confirms Annan, Dumfries and Galloway (Lowland), owned by the Annandale Distillery Company (David Thomson and Teresa Church since 2007). Corrected peatProfile from the seed's "medium" to "light": a detailed independent review of the Double Oak and STR Cask releases (greatdrams.com) describes the smoke as "subtle" and explicitly "rather than heavily peated", against one unsourced aggregator claim of "heavily peated" that no opened page corroborated.
Confirmed via Redwood Empire's own site: "Pipe Dream Bourbon", one of its everyday releases. No peat/smoke mentioned. Parented to the new "redwood-empire" row added in this batch's producer.tsv.

Verified via own site: Glurns, Venosta Valley, South Tyrol, Italy, "The Italian Malt Whisky". Every current range (Core: GOLD/SOLE/VINA; ARTE; and others) is described with fruit/vanilla/honey/oak notes and no peat or smoke anywhere.

Reconfirmed directly via Orkney Distilling's own product page: peated blended malt Scotch whisky sourced from distilleries across Scotland including Orkney; nose "intriguing smokiness", palate "gentle peat smoke", finish "light smokiness" -- a light, not heavy, peat level.

Reconfirmed via Wikipedia: consumer spirits brand co-founded by actor Sam Heughan and Alex Norouzi in 2021; Sassenach gin was contract-distilled at the Newton Stewart site (formerly Crafty Distillery), acquired by Heughan and Norouzi in 2025 and renamed Galloway Distillery, with whisky/vodka production being brought in-house there too. No peat mentioned. Kept kind=blend and parentSlug empty rather than asserting single-origin, matching the seed's deliberate caution -- a human reviewer should confirm whether current Sassenach whisky stock is entirely Galloway-distilled before promoting this to kind=brand with parentSlug=galloway. Raised confidence to high since the facts actually asserted here (identity, country, owner) are solidly verified; only the withheld parent link is uncertain.

Confirmed via scotchwhisky.com's whiskypedia (opened this session): Glen Ord distillery, Muir of Ord, Highland, owned by Diageo since 1997; The Singleton of Glen Ord is its Asia-focused single malt, launched 2006. Corrected peatProfile from the seed's "none": the same source states the malt carries "low levels of peat smoke" -- since that is not the producer's own domain, not asserting a positive level either; keeping unknown and flagging for a human reviewer to check Diageo's own materials directly.

The seed found no web presence; this session identified a strong match: "Akashi Takumi Blended Whisky" (30% malted barley/70% grain, aged in American oak then sherry-cask finished), from the Akashi brand of Eigashima Shuzo's White Oak distillery (row eigashima, this batch) -- flavour described as "rich, smooth and fruity", no peat/smoke. Linked as parentSlug=eigashima. Flagging for human review: the catalogue's bare "Takumi" listing is inferred to be this product (also a generic word meaning "artisan" used by unrelated brands, e.g. Kentucky Owl Takumi Edition bourbon, hence alias kept at brand scope only per the seed's own reasoning) -- worth confirming against the actual scraped listing.

Reconfirmed via own site: Lovingston, VA, American Single Malt whisky, self-described as "the most awarded single malt whisky distillery in America". No peat/smoke statement found and no peated expression known in their range.

Glenmorangie ownership (The Glenmorangie Company, an LVMH subsidiary since 2004), Tain, Highland, confirmed via Wikipedia. Unlike the seed's two 403s, this session confirmed the Westport pseudonym itself directly via whiskipedia.com: "Westport (Glenmorangie with a teaspoon Glen Moray)" -- a teaspooned Glenmorangie. peatProfile=none per Glenmorangie's well-documented unpeated house style. parentSlug=glenmorangie refers to the already-live producer (confirmed present in live-slugs.txt), so no new row is needed for it here.

new row for lost-monarch, pipe-dream. Verified via own site: founded by Derek Benham (company founded 2013, distilling from 2015) in Graton, CA (Russian River Valley); distills in-house (Master Distiller Jeff Duckhorn) and has historically also sourced mature whiskey to complement its own distillate; relocated to Mare Island, Vallejo in 2025 (acquired Savage & Cooke). Produces Pipe Dream Bourbon, Colonel Armstrong Bourbon, Emerald Giant Rye, Lost Monarch Blend and others (mixed types, so defaultTypeName left empty); no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere on the site.
